text:
alice: Heads-up: starting staged rollout of v2 header normalization shim at 17:30 UTC. This is the multi-tenant path (not mobile-only). Please eyeballs.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: v2-header-shim / stage=canary / target=10% traffic / start=2024-07-12T17:30Z. Watch deploybot logs: https://deploys.internal/redwood/12345
ben: Quick Q — does the shim change header case or add a new header key? clients that do case-sensitive routing might break.
alice: It folds case to lowercase and preserves original header in X-Orig-API-Version. Not adding new keys besides X-Orig-API-Version.
carol: Noted. Can we add a short compatibility note to release notes for integrators? Saw a couple of tenants with strict proxy rules.
release-manager: I'll add a blurb before rollout: "v2 header normalization: requests to the gateway will be casefolded; integrators relying on exact-case matching must pin to v1 or update routing."
dave: Oncall pls: if we see 503s from edge for specific tenants, is the plan to pin them out or rollback global?
sre-oncall: We'll triage. If it's a small set, we can pin tenants to v1 and keep rollout. If >5% or cross-region, consider pause+rollback. Thresholds in runbook: cpu/5xx spike >2x baseline AND sustained 5m -> pause.
ben: Can deploy-bot add a canary probe to check a sample tenant list? Some tenants use older proxies.
alice: Added a quick probe list to deploy config: `prober.tenants: [tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma, tenant-legacy]`
deploy-bot: Canary probes running every 30s. Current status: tenant-alpha OK, tenant-gamma latency +8ms, tenant-legacy 200 from proxy at 17:35:14 (502).
carol: Tenant-legacy 502s — probable proxy doesn't like casefold. Can we pin tenant-legacy immediately?
sre-oncall: Pinning now: `deploybot pin-tenant --tenant tenant-legacy --route v1` -> success. Traffic diverted.
dave: Thanks. Does that leave rollout healthy to continue to 25%?
alice: Let's hold at 10% for another 10m while we scan logs and update release notes. Also ops-eyes.
release-manager: Updated release notes and posted to #release-notes-diff. Added mitigation steps and tenant pin procedure.
ben: Small ask: can we add a telemetry flag for header-normalize-fallback so we can count requests that hit the shim?
alice: Yep, toggled `telemetry.header_normalize` for canary. We'll have token-level breakdown in console.
deploy-bot: Canary progressed to 15% at 17:42Z (after manual approval). Prober status: green for probe tenants.
sre-oncall: Observability looks OK: 4xx/5xx stable, tail latency +3ms. None of the top 50 tenants impacted.
dave: If we see any cross-region degradation, we'll pause and run rollback. Operator checklist ready.
carol: When we flip to 50% do we want a rollout note to send to the embedded-platform teams? A few infra PRs expect exact header casing in the short term.
release-manager: I'll send a short note at 50% and tag platform-team and mobile-eng.
alice: Plan: 10% -> 30% after 20m hold -> 50% after another 20m -> full in 6h if stable. Rollback criteria: >2x 5xx baseline OR tenant pin rate >0.5% of traffic OR user-reported major regressions.
dave: Approved from ops. @deploy-bot keep me in the loop if any auto-pauses trigger.
deploy-bot: Will notify channel and create incident if auto-pause.
carol: One more thing — add a short code snippet for partners to pin: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/pin -d '{"tenant":"TENANT","route":"v1"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'```
release-manager: Included the snippet in release notes. Also added rollback playbook link.
sre-oncall: No further anomalies in 25m. Recommend progressing to 30% at operator discretion.
alice: Moving to 30% now. Sending operator handback at 30% point. :eyes:
ben: Thanks all — will monitor SDK clients for case-sensitive header parsing bugs.
carol: Posting a follow-up doc with example nginx proxy snippet to tolerate header case.
dave: Great. If anything spikes, we revert to v1 route pin for affected tenants.
release-manager: Final: logging summary stored at https://logs.internal/redwood/rollout/1790001234-summary. Will close thread when fully stable or rolled back. :white_check_mark:
